content.value_statement: CI failures slow delivery when logs are noisy and test errors are unclear. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code analyze logs, choose a fix path, and verify tests.
actual_capabilities: Routes CI analysis requests to the failure analysis guide.
Routes test repair requests to the failing test repair guide.
Suggests commands for viewing recent GitHub Actions failure logs.
Classifies build, dependency, environment, and test failures.
Recommends verification steps after test or implementation fixes.
Requires approval before changing tests or CI settings when needed.
limitations: It depends on available CI logs and repository context.
It does not guarantee that every pipeline failure can be fixed automatically.
It can run local test commands only when the project supports them.
It should not bypass tests, lint rules, or required CI checks.

use_cases.title: Investigate Failed Runs
use_cases.description: Review CI logs, identify the first meaningful error, and explain the likely cause.

use_cases.title: Repair Failing Tests
use_cases.description: Compare failing tests with implementation behavior and propose a safe fix path.

use_cases.title: Review Pipeline Health
use_cases.description: Classify recurring CI failures and decide whether code, tests, or environment settings need attention.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Failed Run
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a failed CI job.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this CI failure. Use the run log I provide, identify the first root error, and suggest the next action.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Test Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer needs a readable explanation before editing code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this failing test output and explain whether the problem is implementation, test expectation, or environment setup.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Failing Test Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer wants an implementation change with verification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix the failing test without skipping checks. Prefer implementation changes, explain any test changes, and run targeted verification.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Repeated CI Repairs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow after several failed repair attempts.
prompt_templates.prompt: The CI repair loop has failed twice. Summarize the attempts, isolate remaining failures, and propose a staged recovery plan.

output_examples.input: The latest GitHub Actions run failed during the build step.
output_examples.output: The likely root cause is a TypeScript build error before tests start. Review the first compiler error, fix the affected import or type, then rerun the build job.

output_examples.input: A unit test expects one value but receives another after a recent change.
output_examples.output: The failure needs a specification check. If the new behavior is intended, update the expectation with approval. If not, fix the implementation and rerun the targeted test.

output_examples.input: Several tests fail after a dependency update.
output_examples.output: Start with dependency resolution and setup errors before changing tests. Confirm the lockfile, install step, and mocked interfaces before running the full suite.

best_practices: Share the failed job log, run identifier, and recent changes when possible.
Fix implementation and configuration issues before changing test expectations.
Run targeted tests first, then run the full suite before reporting completion.
anti_patterns: Skipping tests to make CI pass.
Removing assertions without confirming product requirements.
Disabling lint or CI checks instead of fixing the root cause.

faq.question: Does this skill support GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for listing runs and viewing failed GitHub Actions logs.

faq.question: Does this skill support GitLab CI?
faq.answer: It can analyze GitLab CI logs when you provide the failed job output and repository context.

faq.question: Can it edit tests?
faq.answer: Yes, but it should prefer implementation fixes and request approval when test expectations may be outdated.

faq.question: Can it run commands?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed for tools that can read files and run CI or test commands with user oversight.

faq.question: Will it bypass CI checks?
faq.answer: No. The guidance prohibits skipping tests, removing assertions, or disabling required checks as a normal fix.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the failed job log, run identifier, affected files, and any recent changes related to the failure.
